description_full: Hitachi, Ltd. provides digital system and services, green energy and mobility, and connective industry solutions in Japan and internationally. It operates through Digital Systems & Services, Energy, Mobility, Connective Industries, and Others segments. The company offers system integration, consulting, cloud services, storage, servers, software, and ATMs; finance solutions, social infrastructure information systems, public IT solutions, industrial internet of things, digital engineering, control system, and cloud services; and IT products, such as data management and storage. It also provides energy power grids, clean, nuclear, renewable energy, transmission, distribution, digital service, service and consulting, and utility solutions; and railway systems, such as rolling stock, signaling, supervision, telecommunications, and ticketing and payment solutions; automotive automation, including automotive assembly, glass applications, press automation, powertrain, paint and sealer applications, and tyre and wheel systems; and e-mobility solutions, as well as elevators and escalators, home appliances, air conditioners, industry and distribution solution, water and environment solutions, and industrial machinery. In addition, the company offers semiconductor manufacturing equipment; electron microscopes and atomic force microscopes; analytical systems, such as spectrophotometers, thermal analysis and chromatography systems, x-ray fluorescence analyzers, silicon drift detectors, potentiometric titrator, laser induced breakdown spectroscopy, and magnetic induction devices; clinical analyzers, and treatment and diagnostics solutions. Further, it provides automated manufacturing and robotic technologies, industrial & portable air compressors, industrial equipment systems, build-to-order industrial equipment, water environment solution, ATM and cash recycling. Hitachi, Ltd. was founded in 1910 and is headquartered in Tokyo, Japan.

financial_summary: Hitachi Ltd. is a large-cap industrials business with a $129.9B market cap on $96.7B of annual revenue.
The business throws off $5.5B in free cash flow — roughly 6 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders.
Accruals are elevated at -10.2% of assets, and Sloan showed firms building earnings through accruals rather than cash systematically underperform.
On the balance sheet, debt is moderate at 3.9× net debt/EBITDA, serviceable in normal conditions but worth watching through a downturn, and thin 2.6× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.
Net dilution runs at 2.1% annually, transferring value from owners to stock-based comp, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome.
